title: Sell Mineral Rights in Troy, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Troy, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Troy in Bradford County? We buy dry-gas Marcellus interests directly from families with honest cash offers.
heroLead: Troy sits in a part of Bradford County that turned from dairy farming to gas country almost overnight during the boom years, and a lot of families here still measure time by which came first, the milk check or the royalty check.
intro: Troy is a small borough in northern Bradford County, historically known for dairy farming, in a part of the county that saw intense Marcellus leasing activity starting around 2008. The dry-gas fairway runs directly through this area, and operators pursued long-term leases aggressively enough that a significant share of farmland around Troy ended up under contract within just a few years.

For dairy families especially, the arrival of gas leasing changed the financial picture of a farm substantially, sometimes providing income that outpaced the dairy operation itself. That shift also meant a lot of families signed leases quickly, during a period when legal guidance on post-production deduction language wasn't always readily available.

sections.heading: From Dairy Income to Gas Income
paragraphs: A lot of Troy-area farms have depended on both dairy and gas income for over a decade now, and as dairy margins have tightened in recent years, mineral income has become a more central part of some families' financial picture. That makes understanding your royalty statement, and what it might be worth to sell outright, more important than ever.

sections.heading: Checking Whether Your Lease Still Reflects a Fair Deal
paragraphs: If your family's lease was signed early in the boom, it's worth comparing the post-production deduction language against what newer leases typically include. Older leases often allow broader deductions, which Kilmer v. Elexco has generally upheld, and that gap between gross and net value tends to be larger on these earlier agreements.

faqs.question: Does gas income affect farm-related tax situations for a dairy operation?
faqs.answer: It can, and it's worth discussing with your own accountant or tax advisor, since royalty income is treated differently than farm income in some respects.

faqs.question: Is Marcellus development still active around Troy?
faqs.answer: Many units in this area continue producing steadily from wells drilled during the original boom. We check current DEP data against your specific parcel to confirm what applies to you.

faqs.question: What if my farm still has an active dairy operation? Does that complicate a mineral sale?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Selling your mineral rights has no effect on your surface farming operation, and the two can be handled completely independently.

faqs.question: How do I confirm whether my old lease is still held by production?
faqs.answer: Check the habendum clause against whether a well within your unit has kept producing. If it has, most standard leases from the boom years remain in force indefinitely.
